facts.raw_span: A patient in their 70s
medical history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension
presented to the emergency department with fatigue, light-headedness, and dyspnea on exertion during the previous week
heart rate of 47 beats per minute
blood pressure of 148/59 mm Hg
Normal sinus rhythm at 72 beats per minute
PR interval prolongs between first and second conducted beats
Some P waves do not conduct to ventricles
Right bundle-branch block present
Prolonged His-ventricular (HV) interval of 75 milliseconds on first conducted beat, extending to 277 milliseconds on second conducted beat
Normal biventricular function without significant valvular lesions
Surface ECG showed sinus rhythm

concepts.why: The patient's ECG findings show normal sinus rhythm with PR interval prolongation and some P waves not conducting to ventricles, which is consistent with Sick Sinus Syndrome.
The patient's ECG findings show a right bundle-branch block, which is a characteristic finding of this condition.
The patient's ECG findings show a prolonged PR interval, which is consistent with First-Degree AV Block.
The patient has a history of hypertension and presented with high blood pressure, which is consistent with Hypertensive Heart Disease.
The patient has a history of type 2 diabetes, which is a risk factor for Diabetic Cardiomyopathy.

rationales.F04: The patient's heart rate of 47 beats per minute is a strong indicator of Sick Sinus Syndrome.
rationales.F08: Some P waves not conducting to ventricles is a strong indicator of both Sick Sinus Syndrome and First-Degree Atrioventricular (AV) Block.
rationales.F10: The prolonged His-ventricular interval is a strong indicator of both Sick Sinus Syndrome and First-Degree Atrioventricular (AV) Block.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's ECG findings, including PR interval prolongation and some P waves not conducting to ventricles, along with the electrophysiology study showing a prolonged His-ventricular interval, strongly support First-Degree Atrioventricular (AV) Block as the most specific diagnosis.
